label: Slytherin
source_text: Sorting Hat's song (Philosopher's Stone, ch. 7), quoted in Wizarding World's 'The Wizarding Songbook' (2015-12-09, https://www.harrypotter.com/features/the-wizarding-songbook-hogwarts-greatest-hits): "Or perhaps in Slytherin / You'll make your real friends, / Those cunning folk use any means / To achieve their ends." Goblet of Fire song, quoted by the Harry Potter Lexicon (https://www.hp-lexicon.org/thing/sorting-hat-songs/, 'Harry's Fourth Year'): "And power-hungry Slytherin / loved those of great ambition". Wizarding World house feature (2021-04-28): "ambitious, shrewd and possibly destined for greatness"; "is always one step ahead, has a dark sense of humour, thinks reputation is important, takes pride in their appearance and doesn't let anyone see their soft side". Official fact file: "characters defined by cunning, pride and ambition". Wikipedia: "values ambition, cunning, leadership, and resourcefulness."
description_draft: This means being ambitious, shrewd, cunning and proud, always one step ahead and using any means to achieve one's ends, minding one's reputation, and never letting anyone see one's soft side.
nearest_existing: ambitious / ends_justify_means / calculating / scheming / guarded: the typed version is the house portrait, ambition and cunning worn with pride and a guarded front, and the Hat's 'any means' now puts it beside ends_justify_means and calculating; it differs in being a whole character (reputation, pride, the hidden soft side, the 'real friends' of one's own house) rather than a single moral stance, and the source still does not call it villainy.
notes: Sharpened toward the books at Roger's request (2026-10-07): the Hat's 'use any means to achieve their ends' is now in the description, displacing the 2021 feature's 'dark sense of humour' and 'pride in appearance' for length; 'possibly destined for greatness' is still dropped. The Hat's line was found on the official site's 2015 songbook feature and on the Harry Potter Lexicon's songs page (whose transcription reads 'cunning folks', plural; the official site has 'cunning folk', which is used); Wikipedia's Hogwarts article (and its Slytherin redirect), the 'Magical objects in Harry Potter' article and Wikiquote's Philosopher's Stone, Goblet of Fire and Order of the Phoenix pages carry no Sorting Hat lines; Fandom returns 402. The Goblet of Fire line is recorded from the Lexicon only, since the official page does not carry it. Strength: now at the books' level, markedly less flattering than the other three houses' drafts, which stay at the official site's level; the set keeps its shape (virtues, behaviours, shadow) but Slytherin now carries two shadows (any means; hidden soft side). Supersedes the 'flagged, not done' remark in the Hogwarts set_review on gryffindor in drafts_d3_sets.json. The other three houses are unchanged. 31 words. US spelling throughout (no 'humour' remains in the draft).
